routes.name: DAAD RISE
routes.funding: Monthly stipend, insurance and travel support
routes.detail: Paired with a German doctoral student on a STEM project for two to three months. Applications typically open in November and close in December or January.

routes.name: Amgen Scholars Program
routes.detail: Eight to ten weeks in a research university laboratory across the life sciences, chemistry, engineering and related fields.

routes.name: Caltech SURF
routes.detail: A ten-week mentored research placement. Strong fit if you already have a specific laboratory or topic in mind.

routes.name: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU)
routes.detail: Hundreds of funded summer projects across science and engineering. Most sites require US citizenship or permanent residency, so read eligibility carefully.

routes.name: FindAPhD
routes.funding: Listed per project, usually fees plus stipend
routes.detail: The largest directory of advertised doctoral projects. Search by topic and check whether funding covers international fees.

routes.name: EURAXESS
routes.detail: The European Commission's portal for research positions, funding calls and mobility advice, including visa and family support.

routes.name: NRF South Africa
routes.detail: The National Research Foundation funds postgraduate study through universities. Applications usually run mid-year for the following academic year.

routes.name: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS)
routes.detail: A one-year, pan-African master's with a strong research and industry placement record. Applications are open to graduates across Africa.

routes.name: TWAS
routes.detail: Fellowships for scientists from developing countries, often hosted by partner institutions in countries such as China, Brazil and India.

routes.name: African Academy of Sciences
routes.detail: Programmes such as DELTAS Africa and Affiliates support early-career African researchers and research leaders.

routes.name: MITACS Globalink Research Internship
routes.detail: Twelve weeks in a Canadian laboratory for students from partner countries, usually applied for in the preceding September to February.

routes.name: CERN Summer Student Programme
routes.detail: Work alongside researchers in physics, engineering or computing. A working knowledge of programming or detector physics helps your application.

guide.step: Decide what you want from research
guide.detail: Be specific about whether you want a short summer project, a paid research assistantship, a master's by research or a full PhD. Each has a different entry route and a different application conversation.

guide.step: Read two or three papers in the field
guide.detail: Choose recent papers by researchers at universities you can realistically reach. You are looking for methods you understand and a gap you can describe in one sentence, not for a complete literature review.

List your relevant coursework, any project you completed, software or lab skills, and one concrete result such as a grade, a poster or a working prototype. Supervisors scan for whether you can start contributing on day one.
Name their paper, say what interested you in it, state what you can do and ask for a short meeting or whether they have space. Two short paragraphs, no attachments beyond a one-page CV.

guide.step: Apply to structured programmes in parallel
guide.detail: Cold emails have a low response rate. Run them alongside formal routes such as DAAD RISE, Amgen Scholars, NRF bursaries or advertised PhD projects so one silence does not end your search.

guide.step: Turn the work into a credential
guide.detail: Ask early about authorship, poster sessions and conference support. A completed project, a reference letter and a presentation are what make the next application stronger.
